claims.statement: Every nontrivial zero rho of zeta satisfies Re(rho)=1/2.
The existing c=2 trace/Frobenius/positive-index certificate is simultaneously extremal on online doubles and tight off-line pairs and cannot be improved using only those quantities.

For an absolutely summable spectral zero filter with critical-line center, any zeta zero with Re(rho) > 1/2 and nonzero multiplicity-weighted filter coefficient forces the filtered zero family to fail the subexponential bound (exposed right-side Laplace pole). Left-side zeros are excluded downstream via the zeta reflection rho -> 1 - conj(rho), never by imposing reflection symmetry on generic filters.

The filtered zero family of the natural Weil filter at center 1/2 equals, at every aperture a, the literature explicit-formula RHS of the right-translated test k(. - 2a), under exact C^2 compact-support hypotheses; absolute filter summability follows from EF_lit's summability clause.

For every hypothetical zeta zero strictly to the right of the critical line there exists an admissible pole-killed C^2 compactly supported Weil test (target-adaptive modulated bump through the pole-killer q'' - q/4) whose translated literature-RHS residual fails the subexponential bound.

claims.statement: The translated pole-killed Weil residual family is subexponential from unconditional arithmetic/prime-side estimates (scalar form: Zeta23.ExceptionalZero.ArithmeticSideSubexponential).
claims.note: Proved logically equivalent to C_RH itself (see R001_PRIME_UPPER_EQUIV_RH and OBS-008). Must not be attacked as an independent arithmetic estimate; any closure is RH-strength by theorem.

claims.statement: The scalar-class R001 prime-side target ArithmeticSideSubexponential is logically equivalent to RH for the zeta zero configuration: it implies RH via the exposed-pole detector with reflection, and RH implies it via unit-modulus critical-line modes.

Block-level separation via the negative-index channel: the exact off-line pair block c*(x x^T - y y^T) of ZeroSide.pair_term, with positive weight and transverse real parts (nonzero Gram determinant), admits an explicit direction on which its Hermitian form is strictly negative (value exactly -c*gramDet^2), and is therefore not equal to any nonnegatively weighted sum of real rank-one blocks - the shape of every on-line configuration and of the TightMult extremal mock. The separating quantity is not a function of the trace/Frobenius/on-line-atom/positive-index data of OBS-001.

claims.statement: The negative direction of an off-line pair block survives the positive-semidefinite on-line bulk in a full probe window, so that lambda_min of the windowed Gram is negative whenever an off-line zero lies in the window.
claims.note: Feasibility bookkeeping (routes/R002_multi_probe/MULTI_PROBE_GRAM_OPERATOR_FEASIBILITY_2026_08_21.md) gives visibility iff delta*L >~ sqrt(6/lambda), with every-delta detection in the oversampled regime lambda>1; the price is X=e^L>T on the prime side.

claims.statement: For the theorem-authoritative finite CCM matrix on centered Fourier indices and positive aperture L, the index commutator is exactly g 1^T - 1 g^T and therefore has rank at most two.

Displacement transfer algebra over C: D*M - M*D is unchanged by adding a scalar matrix c*I, hence if A = k*M + c*I and D*M - M*D = g 1^T - 1 g^T then D*A - A*D = k*(g 1^T - 1 g^T) and rank(D*A - A*D) <= 2. This is what carries the exact finite CCM displacement identity onto a target matrix once an exact scaled-scalar-shift identity is supplied; that identity is an explicit hypothesis here.

For every N, every real centered-grid coefficient vector u and every aperture L>0, the rank-one-regularized finite-dictionary residual has a complex-valued wrapper that is C^2 and compactly supported, exactly satisfying the regularity hypotheses used by EF_lit.
claims.note: This proves admissibility only for the smooth residual r_{u,L}. The full dictionary also contains the canonical tent sigma(u)^2*tau_L, whose explicit-formula extension remains open. No restriction sum(u)=0 is used.

claims.statement: For every L>0, the canonical tent tau_L has its exact paperFT closed form with removable value L, obeys theorem-authoritative quadratic decay on |Im z|<=1/2 in multiplied form, and its transform is absolutely summable over the concrete zeta zero configuration with multiplicity.
claims.note: Transform, strip decay and zero-side summability only. This does not extend EF_lit to the nonsmooth tent and does not identify the tent zero sum with literatureRHS.

claims.statement: For every aperture L>0, the canonical dictionary tent admits the repository's normalized shrinking mollifier family whose members are C^2, share a common physical support envelope independent of the mollifier index, converge pointwise to the literal canonical tent, satisfy an exact complex-frequency paperFT convolution factorization, and inherit a uniform quadratic transform bound on |Im z|<=1/2.
claims.note: This is the Route-M M0-M3 adapter architecture only. It does not pass EF_lit_zeta to the nonsmooth literal tent and proves no pole, prime, archimedean, or varying-family zero-side limit exchange. R003_TENT_EF_EXTENSION remains OPEN.

The production dictionary carries a factor 1/2, so the theorem target is finiteMatrix(L,N)+2*cCorrection(L)*I, not the older doubled diagnostic normalization. This does not prove the tent explicit-formula extension, any zero-side matrix identity, positivity, a finite-to-infinite theorem, or RH.
